FN-KH6YSAU-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 94
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Tim Melson
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 01/20/2026
Senate Bill 94 as introduced would eliminate existing civil fines for the unauthorized use of a
designated disability access parking place and establish a criminal penalty and fines for the
unauthorized use of these parking places, beginning in FY 2027. This could increase or decrease
receipts to municipal and county general funds, the Administrative Office of Courts (AOC), the
Department of Mental Health (DMH) and respective state law enforcement agencies, by
undetermined amounts dependent upon the difference in civil fines currently collected and the
criminal fines collected pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Beginning in FY 2029, this bill would decrease receipts, collected from criminal fines, by an
undetermined amount to municipal and county general funds and would correspondingly
increase receipts to the AOC and DMH, by revising the distribution of proceeds from the
criminal fines collected for the unauthorized use of these parking places by issuing local law
enforcement agencies.
This bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal
general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the
obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined
amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses
provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.

FN-KH6YSAU-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 94
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Senator Tim Melson
Security
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 02/24/2026
Senate Bill 94 as passed the Senate would increase the administrative obligations of the
Department of Revenue to implement an electronic scannable code system for disability
placards. This bill would not otherwise affect state or local funding.
